Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $35 million class fund, distributed automatically to the members Brightline can identify from its records. Brightline would separately pay up to $2.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would go to the class. This structure prioritizes payments to members and avoids a claims process.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments and a straightforward fee structure are important. Brightline can offer a $31 million class fund plus up to $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can narrow the remaining gap: a $33 million class fund, with the $2 million fee provision and all other terms as you proposed.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic payments and the fee structure. To close the remaining gap, Brightline offers a $32 million class fund and $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. To resolve the remaining $1 million difference, we propose a $32.5 million class fund. We accept your other terms: automatic payments, up to $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $32.5 million class fund with automatic distribution, up to $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery while leaving room to negotiate given certification and trial risks. Automatic payments are feasible and more valuable to members than a claims-made process. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any reduction to the class.

The $37.5 million proposal is within authorization and has a strong approval structure, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Preserve automatic distribution and fee terms that support court approval.

The $31 million automatic class fund is a strong offer given trial and certification risks, but there is room to seek a modest improvement without compromising the class-friendly structure. Keep fees at defense's figure and avoid fee-related tradeoffs.

Their $35 million total offer is within authority and has a strong approval structure. A modest counteroffer could save $1 million while preserving the automatic distribution and fee terms; several rounds remain.

The $32 million automatic-distribution fund is strong relative to the trial-risk-adjusted recovery, but the parties are only $1 million apart and have three rounds remaining. A modest midpoint counteroffer could increase direct class recovery without jeopardizing the agreed protective terms.
The proposed $34.5 million total is well within authorization, preserves automatic distribution and court-approval-friendly fee terms, and resolves litigation risk. Accept.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As interim class counsel, Hargrove Lane LLP supports preliminary approval. The settlement followed three rounds of arm’s-length negotiations. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were addressed together, not in separate sequential phases. The parties agreed to a $32.5 million fund for approximately 400,000 identifiable members, distributed automatically without a claim form. Brightline will separately pay up to $2 million in court-approved fees and expenses; it has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any amount not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The fund represents approximately 51% of the $64 million in disputed charges. In our judgment, this substantial, prompt recovery is fair in light of the unresolved certification question, the risk of no recovery at trial, and the expected two-to-three-year wait for trial. Counsel’s compensation is fixed and does not depend on the settlement fee award. We request preliminary approval, subject to notice, objections, and the Court’s final review.
